page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The server is provisioned with 2 vCPUs utilizing a shared CPU allocation model, 2 physical cores, and 1.0 thread per core. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and there are no GPUs. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that this server operates primarily in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 783.18 and 1545.08 respectively, placing both in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with large-block read bandwidth at 12.62 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 10.18 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. However, certain workloads demonstrate moderate capability; the Geekbench single-core score of 1862.0 and text processing score of 2215.0 both rank in the middle 50%, as does the single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 8.99 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and modest memory capacity, this server represents a budget-oriented tier designed for resource-efficient utility. The tradeoff of shared CPU resources and lower memory bandwidth limits its suitability for intensive database operations or high-throughput web serving, as reflected in the static web serving throughput of 2.15 GB/sec and Passmark database score of 1356.4. It is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic text processing, simple single-threaded tasks, or low-demand development and testing environments where high compute density is not required.
